note: CLOSED-LOOP PROOF, because the renderer's verdict is wrong for a quantised cycle. It reports wrap 1.7068% vs mean step 0.6493%, ratio 2.629 -> 'open drift at the wrap'. Ran at(0) and at(1) in node: IDENTICAL ({index:0, angle:-pi/2, on:true, force:1, within:0}). Counted the tap transitions: 16 of the 48 adjacent pairs carry one, so the mean adjacent step is diluted 48/16 = 3.00x and a ratio just under 3 is the exact signature of a closed cycle that changes state on one pair in three. A ratio near 1.0 here would mean the tap had been SMOOTHED, which MOTION-BRIEF names as a punishable failure.

note: BF-14 landed while Act II was being written, and it shipped assets/set/_tap-ring.mjs — a second module for the same figure, with a header addressed to this scene: 'BF-21 imports it', 'BF-21: match these or say why'. Mine (assets/set/_tapping.mjs) had a header addressed to theirs. Two modules for one figure is exactly the failure the shared-authoring rule exists to prevent. DELETED mine and converged on theirs. Where the conventions disagreed, theirs wins and is right: dwell 0.50 not 0.72 (their arithmetic — at 0.72 only one of six frames per station is in transit, so 62% of the gap is covered across the WRAP and the renderer reports drift on a closed loop; I re-derived it for my own 48/8 and got the same number, which is what their decision 2 asks a consumer to do); contact decays 1->0 over 34% of the dwell at ARRIVAL rather than being a flat rectangle ('a tap that fades IN is a caress' — mine faded neither way, which made it a light rather than a strike); and struck[] accumulates the stations visited and resets at the wrap, which I had nothing like and which is the best idea in either file. Both files independently put station 0 at the far side running clockwise, so that never needed deciding. What survived from my side is the DRAWING, which is a scene's business.

note: SECOND DUPLICATION FOUND, AND NOT CONSOLIDATED — declared rather than hidden. Act I landed _lens.mjs while this act was being written; it is the same affine-over-project() idea with a different signature (centre station NAME + an `at` pixel, vs centre in plan-projected coordinates). Same transform, same declared x-by-width / y-by-height asymmetry, same guarantee. The one real difference is a constant: _lens.mjs sets BODY = 300px per unit of project() scale at zoom 1; _stage.mjs derives BODY_H = 0.62 x frame height = 471px from BF-01's maze geometry. Not a continuity error in any frame — both acts apply a further per-scene factor and the plan supplies the relative sizes — but two unnormalised body constants in one world should be one. NOT consolidated: doing it at the end of an act means re-deriving the framing of fourteen rendered scenes for no visible gain, and unlike the tap ring this is not a drawing two scenes have to share. Logged in the module header and in the act report so it is a decision and not an oversight.
